Ravana's Sons and Last Generals

Stories from the Ramayana

Ravana's Sons and Last Generals

After Kumbhakarna, Ravana's sons and his last generals

In everyday English — Yuddha Kanda, sargas 69–72, 76–79, 93–98

Stories by Eku

How to Read · · BEFORE WE BEGIN

Read it out loud. This story is made to be told. Read slowly, as if you are sitting with everyone at home.

This book is the war's heaviest story — Ravana's sons come, and fall. Where there is a duel, quicken your voice; where a killing comes, grow slow and grave — never shout.

The yellow boxes hold the characters' own words. Change your voice a little as you speak them — Ravana grieving, Sugriva praising, Lakshmana firm.

(Purple hints) tell you where to pause, whisper, or raise your voice. They are for the reader — do not read them aloud.

The green box at the end of each part — Pause and think. Stop there. Ask questions. Let the listeners speak.

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 69–72, 76–79, 93–98 — the fall of Ravana's sons and last generals, and the lament of Lanka's women. The parts that speak of killing carry the ◆ mark at the top. Anything more you may want to know is given separately at the end, in Where This Story Comes From.

Who's Who · · WHO'S WHO

Rama — prince of Ayodhya, bearer of the bow. Warm dark-brown skin, a calm and kind face, fully clothed, barefoot in the forest.

Lakshmana — Rama's younger brother, slightly lighter in complexion, bow in hand. He kills Atikaya with the Brahmastra.

Ravana — king of Lanka. Tall, dark-complexioned, black moustache, tall golden crown, a single head, royal robes. In this book he loses his sons and his brothers.

Sugriva — king of the vanaras, friend of Rama. He kills Kumbha, and Virupaksha and Mahodara.

Hanuman — son of the Wind, minister of Sugriva, messenger of Rama. Light golden-brown fur, long tail, gentle devoted face, saffron dhoti.

Angada — son of Vali, a young vanara warrior. He kills Narantaka and Mahaparshva.

Nila — commander of the vanara army, son of Fire.

Trishira — son of Ravana, a warrior with three heads.

Devantaka — son of Ravana.

Narantaka — son of Ravana, master of the javelin.

Atikaya — son of Ravana and Dhanyamali, a giant warrior wearing armour given by Brahma.

Kumbha and Nikumbha — sons of Kumbhakarna.

Makaraksha — son of Khara, who challenges Rama.

Virupaksha, Mahodara, Mahaparshva — Ravana's last generals and brothers.

1 · The Sons Step Forward · · THE SONS STEP FORWARD

Kumbhakarna was dead — and Ravana was drowned in grief. He wept for his brother — as if his right arm had been cut off.

Then his son Trishira stepped forward and said — “Father, do not weep. We are here — your sons. We will go and kill Rama.”

Hearing Trishira's words, Devantaka, Narantaka and Atikaya also stepped forward — “We will go too!”

Ravana sent them to battle — and sent his brothers Mahodara and Mahaparshva with them, to guard them. A great army marched — elephants, horses, chariots.

The rakshasas shot arrows at the vanaras — and the vanaras raised trees and boulders. The war began again.

Pause and think — Ravana grieves for his brother — and his sons comfort him. Is a son comforting his father also a kind of duty? And when sons go to war — what is in a father's heart — pride or fear?

2 · Narantaka · · NARANTAKA

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it speaks of battle and killing. Elders, please read it gently.

Seeing the rakshasas losing, Narantaka stepped forward — javelin in hand. He killed many vanaras. The vanaras ran in fear to Sugriva.

Sugriva said — “Angada, you go. Only you can fight Narantaka.”

Angada stepped forward. Narantaka hurled his javelin at his chest — but the javelin broke and fell! Angada struck his horse with his hand — and the horse fell.

Then the two fought with their fists — a fist-fight. Angada and Narantaka struck blow upon blow — and at last Narantaka fell.

The gods in the sky and the vanaras on the field cried out Angada's name in victory.

Pause and think — Narantaka's javelin broke on Angada's chest. Was that Angada's strength — or the javelin's weakness? And when a weapon breaks — what does a warrior do — does he fight with his fists?

3 · Trishira and Devantaka · · TRISHIRA AND DEVANTAKA

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it speaks of battle and killing. Elders, please read it gently.

Seeing Narantaka dead, Devantaka, Trishira and Mahodara wept. Then the three fell upon Angada — Devantaka with his iron-spiked club, Mahodara riding an elephant, Trishira on a chariot bright as the sun.

Angada tore up a great tree — and hurled it at Devantaka. Trishira shattered it with his arrows. Angada rained down more trees and boulders — Trishira shattered those too.

Then Hanuman came. He struck Devantaka with his fist — and Devantaka fell. Then he fought Trishira — and Trishira too fell.

As soon as Hanuman killed Trishira, the vanaras roared — the earth shook — and the rakshasa army fled. Mahodara and Mahaparshva drew back — their day was still to come.

Pause and think — Three brothers came together — and two fell. Can brothers standing together still not save one another from defeat? And Hanuman — who had always lifted trees and boulders — why did he fight with his fist this time?

4 · Atikaya · · ATIKAYA

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it speaks of battle and killing. Elders, please read it gently.

Now Atikaya came — son of Ravana and Dhanyamali. His chariot shone like a thousand suns. He was gigantic — like a mountain. He wore armour given by Brahma — and carried a bow and arrows given by Brahma.

Atikaya rained arrows on the vanaras — and no arrow could touch him. Even Rama's arrows struck his armour and fell away. The vanaras began to fear.

Then Vayu, god of the Wind, told Lakshmana — “Lakshmana! Only the Brahmastra can kill this warrior. His armour is Brahma's gift — no other weapon can pierce it.”

Lakshmana called upon the Brahmastra — and set it to his bow. The arrow flew — and even Atikaya's armour could not stop it. Atikaya fell.

When the news reached Ravana — he sank into grief again. Another son was gone.

Pause and think — Atikaya wore Brahma's armour — yet the Brahmastra pierced it. Does every armour have a counter? And why did Vayu show Lakshmana the way — do the gods too take sides in war?

5 · Kumbha · · KUMBHA

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it speaks of battle and killing. Elders, please read it gently.

Now the sons of Kumbhakarna came — Kumbha and Nikumbha. Other rakshasa warriors came with them — Kampana, Prajangha, Sonitaksha, Yupaksha.

Angada killed Kampana and Prajangha. Dvivida killed Sonitaksha. Mainda killed Yupaksha. But Kumbha — alone, he was too much for the vanaras.

Kumbha was a great master of the bow. He shot serpent-like arrows — and the vanaras began to fall. His army's courage rose.

Sugriva stepped forward and said — “Kumbha! Your valour is wonderful — you are equal to Prahlada, Mahabali, Indra and Kubera. With the bow you are equal to Indrajit — and in strength, to your father. Come — let all watch the fight between us.”

Sugriva seized Kumbha's bow and broke it. Then the two fought fiercely — and at last Sugriva killed Kumbha.

Pause and think — Before killing Kumbha, Sugriva praised him — calling him equal to Prahlada and Mahabali. Is praising an enemy also bravery — or is it the rule of war that a hero recognises a hero?

6 · Nikumbha and Makaraksha · · NIKUMBHA AND MAKARAKSHA

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it speaks of battle and killing. Elders, please read it gently.

Seeing his brother Kumbha dead, Nikumbha burned with rage. He raised his gleaming steel club — and advanced toward Sugriva.

Hanuman stepped forward. Nikumbha brought his club down on his chest — and the club shattered into a hundred pieces! Hanuman's chest was unhurt.

Then Hanuman struck Nikumbha with his fist — and Nikumbha fell. The vanaras roared with joy.

When the news reached Ravana — he burned with rage. He called Makaraksha — the son of Khara. Makaraksha saw bad omens — but he did not stop. He challenged Rama — “I will kill you, Lakshmana, Sugriva and all the vanaras!”

Rama and Makaraksha fought fiercely — and at last Rama killed Makaraksha.

Pause and think — Nikumbha's club shattered on Hanuman's chest. Was that Hanuman's strength — or his devotion? And Makaraksha fought despite the bad omens — is the wish for revenge itself a bad omen?

7 · The Last Generals · · THE LAST GENERALS

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it speaks of battle and killing. Elders, please read it gently.

Ravana sent his remaining army — “Go — weaken Rama — so that tomorrow I can kill him.” A great army came — elephants, horses, chariots.

Rama loosed the Gandharvastra — and thousands of rakshasas, elephants and chariots fell. Those who survived fled in fear.

Then Ravana himself came to battle — with his generals. Virupaksha attacked the vanaras — and Sugriva fought him and killed him.

Mahodara too fought — and Sugriva killed him as well. Mahaparshva raised his great club — and Angada fought him and killed him.

Ravana's last generals had fallen. Lanka's army was now almost finished.

Pause and think — Ravana sent the army to weaken Rama — but the army itself was destroyed. Can a plan to weaken someone sometimes weaken oneself instead? And the fall of the last generals — was that the beginning of Lanka's end?

8 · The Women of Lanka Lament · · THE WOMEN OF LANKA LAMENT

Silence lay over the battlefield. In Lanka — in every house — there was weeping. The women whose husbands were dead, whose sons were dead, whose brothers were dead — gathered in one place and began to lament.

They said — “All this happened because of Shurpanakha! That old, ugly rakshasi — why did she go to Rama in the forest? Because of her, Khara and Dushana died — and because of her, Ravana carried off Sita — for his own destruction.”

They said — “Rama killed fourteen thousand rakshasas in Janasthana. He killed Khara and Dushana. He killed Vali. Seeing all this, why did Ravana not listen to Vibhishana's right advice?”

They embraced one another and wept — “Our sons, our brothers, our husbands — all are dead! We have no hope of life left.”

They said — “The gods once asked Shiva for a boon, that a woman would be born for the destruction of the rakshasas. That woman is Sita. This destruction has come because of Ravana's wrongdoing.”

And they knew — Ravana too would be killed. The war was now only a matter of time.

Pause and think — The women did not fight in the war — yet they bore its grief the most. Is it those who never fight who pay the real price of war? And they blamed Shurpanakha and Ravana — was that blame right — or was it the voice of grief?

Where This Story Comes From · · WHERE THIS STORY COMES FROM

Main source

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 69–72, 76–79, 93–98 — the fall of Ravana's sons and last generals.

The sons step forward — sargas 68–69

Ravana's grief for Kumbhakarna; Trishira comforting him; the sons — Trishira, Devantaka, Narantaka, Atikaya — setting out with Mahodara and Mahaparshva — this is in sargas 68–69.

Narantaka — sarga 69

Narantaka killing vanaras with his javelin; Sugriva sending Angada; the javelin breaking on Angada's chest; the horse falling; Narantaka's death in the fist-fight — this is in sarga 69.

Trishira and Devantaka — sarga 70

Hanuman killing Devantaka and Trishira; Mahodara and Mahaparshva fighting and drawing back — this is in sarga 70. The tellings of Devantaka's death differ — see below.

Atikaya — sargas 71–72

Atikaya arriving on a chariot like a thousand suns; no weapon piercing his Brahma-given armour; Vayu telling Lakshmana that only the Brahmastra can kill him; Lakshmana killing him with the Brahmastra; Ravana's grief — this is in sargas 71–72.

Kumbha — sarga 76

The coming of Kumbha and Nikumbha; Angada killing Kampana and Prajangha, Dvivida killing Sonitaksha, Mainda killing Yupaksha; Kumbha the great archer; Sugriva breaking his bow, killing him, and praising him before the fight — this is in sarga 76.

Nikumbha and Makaraksha — sargas 77–79

Nikumbha coming to avenge his brother; his club shattering on Hanuman's chest; Hanuman killing him; Ravana sending Makaraksha; Makaraksha challenging Rama despite the bad omens and being killed by Rama — this is in sargas 77–79.

The last generals — sargas 93, 95–98

Rama destroying the great rakshasa army with the Gandharvastra; Ravana himself coming to battle; Sugriva killing Virupaksha and Mahodara; Angada killing Mahaparshva — this is in sargas 93, 95–98.

The women of Lanka lament — sarga 94

The rakshasa women who have lost husbands, sons and brothers gathering and lamenting; blaming Shurpanakha; remembering Vibhishana's unheeded advice; foretelling Ravana's fall — this is in sarga 94.

About Mahodara and Mahaparshva

In this book Mahodara and Mahaparshva draw back from the battle of sarga 70 — and are killed in the last days, in sargas 97–98, by Sugriva and Angada. Some manuscripts tell their fall in sarga 70 itself — at the hands of Nila and Rishabha — and tell Devantaka's death at Nila's hands too. The telling of sargas 96–98 is followed here as the main one.

About the pictures

This book's pictures show the fighting — but never death, a body, or blood. The pictures show the moment before the fight — the duel before the blow — or the women lamenting. The killing is told only in words.

What happens next

Ravana's sons and generals are now finished. Only his greatest son remains — Indrajit — who is performing a rite at Nikumbhila. The story of Indrajit's illusory Sita is the next book of this series.
